issues.issue: The parties clause names only six parties and omits the Certificate Insurer, yet Article XII and Section 11.12 confer extensive consent, control and payment rights on a Certificate Insurer. Whether the insurer is a party bound by, or merely a beneficiary of, the Agreement must be worked out from the two together.

This preliminary recital states the Trust Fund 'is hereby conveyed to the Trustee,' while the operative conveyance in Section 2.01 makes the transfer subject to delivery of the Mortgage Files and other conditions. A party could argue the recital effects or controls the conveyance notwithstanding Section 2.01.

The direction that 'any inconsistencies or ambiguities in this Agreement' be resolved to preserve the REMIC elections is a general interpretive override whose reach can only be fixed against the rest of the instrument, including the distribution priorities of Section 4.02 and the amendment limits of Section 11.01. It is unclear whether it subordinates express operative terms to tax-driven construction.

Clause (iv) reads 'until the principal balance of such Subsidiary REMIC Regular Interest the Subordinated Portion for Loan Group 3,' omitting the verb 'equals' that appears in every parallel clause. The omission leaves the Group 3 priority without a stated stopping point.

Clause (iv) omits the verb 'equals' ('until the principal balance of such Middle REMIC 1 Regular Interest the Subordinated Portion for Loan Group 3'), unlike the parallel clauses (i)-(v). The Group 3 priority therefore has no stated limit on its face.

This paragraph says the Master REMIC issues a 'Class R-IV Interest' as its sole residual class, but the Preliminary Statement paragraph on certificate interests states that the Class R Certificate represents ownership of the sole residual interest in the Master REMIC. Which instrument evidences the Master REMIC residual cannot be answered from one of the two alone.

The Class X-2 Notional Amount is written '$452,182,00', which is not a well-formed figure and is one digit short of the $452,182,000 implied by the Group 2 balances. The typographical error leaves the initial notional amount uncertain on the face of the provision.

The notional component is defined by reference to 'the aggregate of the Class Principal Amounts of the Middle REMIC 2 Regular Interests,' a term the Agreement does not define (it defines 'Class Principal Balance'). The measure of the Class C notional balance is therefore uncertain.

After enumerating specific classes the definition sweeps in 'in general, any Certificates that do not satisfy the applicable ratings requirement under the Underwriter's Exemption,' a catch-all with no stated boundary against the listed specifics. Whether a class outside the enumeration can be ERISA-Restricted depends on how that residual phrase is read.

The definition is textually truncated — it opens mid-phrase with a stray filing URL and the word 'Certificates' rather than a complete definitional sentence. What term is being defined and its full content cannot be read off the provision itself.

This sentence nullifies unidentified 'defined terms and provisions herein' relating to rating agencies other than Moody's, S&P and Fitch, so its effect can only be determined by running it against every rating-agency reference in the Agreement (for example the rating conditions in Section 11.01 amendments). Which provisions it strikes is not visible from its own words.

Accrual Period is defined only for the Delay Certificates and the No Delay Certificates, but the Preliminary Statement provides that the Class C Certificates accrue interest at a variable Pass-Through Rate and the Class C Certificates fall in neither category. The accrual convention for those classes must be supplied from elsewhere in the instrument.

The definition caps rates at the Pass-Through Rate 'determined without regard to the Available Funds Rate Cap,' but the Preliminary Statement fixes each Pass-Through Rate by reference to the Net Rate Cap, of which the Available Funds Rate Cap is only one input. Reading the two together it is unclear what rate is to be used.

The definition turns on whether a Person 'directly or indirectly controls or is controlled by or is under common control with' another, but 'control' is nowhere defined or given a threshold. The scope of Affiliate is therefore open at its edges.

The phrase 'at the close of business on the related Servicer Remittance Date' is repeated twice in the same sentence, once before and once after the reference to the Mortgage Loan. The duplication garbles what is being measured at that date.

The definition excepts only the Interest Only Certificates from 'the aggregate Class Principal Balance of all Classes of Certificates,' leaving it unclear whether the Class C and Class P Certificates are counted in the comparison. Whether they are counted changes the size of the Applied Realized Loss Amount.

For a Refinancing Mortgage Loan the value is 'the appraisal made at the time of the origination ... as modified by an updated appraisal,' without saying when, by whom or on what standard an updated appraisal is made or whether one is required. The trailing qualifier leaves the value indeterminate.

The definition cross-refers to 'Section 3.22(i)(a),' a subsection designation that does not match the lettering scheme used elsewhere for Section 3.22 (e.g., Section 3.22(b)(i) for the Accountant's Attestation). The referent of the definition must be reconstructed.

The Certificate Insurer becomes Auction Initiator only if the Class C Certificateholder 'has not exercised its rights ... on any date on which [it] is entitled to do so,' but no cut-off date or notice mechanic fixes when that condition is satisfied. Because the right is a continuing one, when it passes to the Certificate Insurer is indeterminate.

The lettering repeats: clause (b) is itself defined as 'the excess, if any, of (a) the Principal Funds ... over (b) the Overcollateralization Release Amount,' reusing (a) and (b) inside limb (b). The nesting error makes the arithmetic of the definition ambiguous on its face.

The list 'banking institutions in the City of New York, New York, Minnesota, Maryland' mixes a city with bare state names and no city, so it is unclear whether closure anywhere in Minnesota or Maryland suffices. The mechanical defect changes which days are Business Days.

The Cap Account is said to be established 'pursuant to 3.07(i) of this agreement,' a citation lacking the word Section and not matching the subsection lettering used for the parallel Carryover Reserve Fund (Section 3.07(h)). The governing subsection has to be located by inference.

This definition has the Certificates executed and authenticated by the Trust Administrator, while Section 11.10 speaks of the Certificates 'upon due authentication thereof by the Trustee pursuant to this Agreement.' Which officer's authentication validates a Certificate cannot be settled from either provision alone.

The Certificate Factor is computed for 'any Class of Regular Certificates' from Certificate Principal Balance, with a parenthetical carve-out only for the Class C Certificates' Notional Amount, yet the definition of Class Principal Balance states that the Interest Only Certificates have no principal balance. For the Class X-1, X-2 and XW Certificates the fraction has no numerator.

The Agreement defines the Certificate Insurance Policy as including 'any endorsements thereto,' while the Policy itself provides that it sets forth in full Financial Security's undertaking and 'shall not be modified, altered or affected by any other agreement or instrument.' Whether the PSA's terms about the Policy can enlarge or qualify the insurer's obligation must be resolved between the two documents.

The Certificate Insurer Fee Rate is subtracted from the Net Rate Cap of the Insured Certificates under the Net Rate Cap definition and is also the measure of the Premium Distribution Amount payable out of the waterfall under Section 4.02. Whether the premium is borne once or twice, and by whom, only emerges from reading those provisions together.

The proviso that an Insured Certificate's Certificate Principal Balance 'shall be deemed not to be reduced by any principal amounts paid to the Holder thereof from payments made by the Certificate Insurer' operates 'solely for purposes of' the Premium Distribution Amount and the insurer's subrogation rights, leaving unclear what the balance is for every other purpose, including loss allocation and voting. The deemed-balance device is the point at which the insurer's and the holders' entitlements diverge.

This definition makes the Holder the person registered in the Certificate Register, but Section 12.01 provides for the Certificate Insurer to exercise the voting rights of the Holders of the Insured Certificates. Who counts as the consenting Holder of an Insured Certificate cannot be answered from this definition alone.

After identifying reimbursement 'with interest' for claims paid, the definition adds 'any amounts with respect to the Class 1-A-3 Certificates owing to the Certificate Insurer and remaining unpaid,' an open-ended catch-all not tied to any enumerated obligation. The class of amounts it sweeps in is unbounded.

The closing phrase 'any amounts with respect to the Class 2-A-3 Certificates owing to the Certificate Insurer and remaining unpaid' is a general catch-all appended to the specific reimbursement-with-interest item. Nothing in the definition limits what obligations qualify as 'owing.'

The clause 'any amounts with respect to the Class 4-A-2 Certificates owing to the Certificate Insurer and remaining unpaid' extends the reimbursement amount beyond the enumerated claims paid under the Policy without any stated boundary. Its scope against the specific preceding item is open to construction.

The Collection Account is maintained by the Master Servicer in its own name, yet the last sentence says it 'may be deemed to be a sub-account of the Distribution Account,' which the Distribution Account definition places with the Trust Administrator in the name of the Trustee. Whose account it is, and on what conditions the deeming operates, requires reading the two definitions together.

The two limbs run together without punctuation ('should be directed With respect to the Trust Administrator'), and the Trust Administrator is given one address 'for certificate transfer purposes' and another 'for all other purposes.' Which office a given notice must reach is left to be sorted out.

The Countrywide Mortgage Loans are identified by loans showing 'Countrywide Home Loans Servicing L.P.' as Servicer, whereas the defined term 'Countrywide' means Countrywide Home Loans, Inc. The two entities are not the same and the definitions do not reconcile them.

The definition is expressed 'solely with respect to the Countrywide Serviced Mortgage Loans,' a term the Agreement never defines (it defines 'Countrywide Mortgage Loans'). The loans to which the Servicing Agreement applies must therefore be inferred.

The fee is computed on 'the Scheduled Principal Balance of the Mortgage Loans,' but the Agreement defines 'Stated Principal Balance' and 'Principal Balance,' not 'Scheduled Principal Balance.' The multiplicand of the fee is undefined.

Current Interest is defined only 'with respect to each Class of Offered Certificates,' yet the Available Funds Rate Cap definition subtracts 'the Current Interest for the Class X-1, Class X-2 and Class XW Certificates,' none of which are Offered Certificates as the Preliminary Statement defines that term. The two provisions cannot both be given their literal effect.

The trigger is 'the product of (i) 28.15% and the Senior Enhancement Percentage for any Distribution Date prior to ... and (ii) 35.15% and the Senior Enhancement Percentage' — a single 'product of' governing two alternative time periods joined by 'and.' Whether the two limbs are alternatives or multiplicands is not clear from the wording.

The definition offers three alternatives (i), (ii) and (iii) but closes clause (iii) with the phrase 'which, in either case,' a two-item qualifier. It is unclear which of the alternatives the fiduciary-capacity requirement attaches to.

Requirement (v) is that the substitute loan 'comply with each representation and warranty set forth in Section 2.03 hereof,' but Section 2.03 is the remedies provision and the loan-level representations and warranties are set out in Schedule II and Section 2.04. The standard a substitute loan must meet is miscited.

The definition refers to the 'No-Delay Certificates,' a hyphenated form that does not match the defined term 'No Delay Certificates' specified in the Preliminary Statement. The class of certificates to which the excluded interest relates is identified only by an undefined variant.

The definition ends by taking in assignments and conveyances 'related to the GMACM Mortgage Loans,' a term the Agreement does not define; the defined term is 'GMACM Serviced Mortgage Loans.' The reach of the incorporated assignments is left uncertain.

The formula reads 'the Net WAC for Loan Group 1 ... minus (1) the sum of Current Interest ... , (2) multiplied by 12, (3) divided by the Stated Principal Balance,' which subtracts a dollar amount from a percentage rate before the annualization and division steps. The order of operations, and hence the cap on the related certificates' Pass-Through Rate, cannot be derived from the words used.

Clause (b) enumerates named categories and then extends to any 'similar loan under any other applicable state, federal or local law' and to loans 'similarly classified ... using different terminology,' a catch-all with no fixed boundary. Whether a given loan falls within it is a question of degree.

The definition identifies the class 'with the highest priority for payments pursuant to Section 4.01,' but Section 4.01 governs Advances and the payment priorities are set out in Section 4.02. The cross-reference points to a section that contains no priority order.

Clause (d) excludes a member of the immediate family of 'a Person defined clause (b) or (c) above,' omitting the preposition and referring to clauses that describe relationships rather than define Persons. The exclusion's referent is garbled.

The definition is circular and unbounded: an Insurance Policy is 'any insurance policy' relating to a Mortgage Loan 'including any replacement policy or policies for any Insurance Policies.' Which policies of the Mortgagor, Servicer or Trust are captured cannot be told from the text.

The amount is computed from 'the Current Interest for such Class' for every Class of Senior and Mezzanine Certificates, but Current Interest is defined only with respect to Classes of Offered Certificates, which exclude the Class M-8 Certificates. For those classes the two definitions do not mesh.

Item (i) deducts 'any payments made in respect of premiums on lender paid insurance mortgage loans,' a garbled phrase that names no identifiable category of payment. What is subtracted from scheduled interest is uncertain.

The definition fixes the rate by reference to 'the then applicable highest rate of interest on the Insured Notes' and to a determination 'by the Class A Note Insurer,' neither of which is a defined term or a party in this Agreement. The rate cannot be computed from the instrument as drafted.

The definition makes the Latest Possible Maturity Date a floating date computed from the Mortgage Loan with the latest scheduled maturity, while the Preliminary Statement tables fix it at December 25, 2046 for every Class. The formula and the tabulated date need not produce the same day.

Limb (i) requires an actual liquidation with all expected recoveries received, while limb (ii) deems any loan '180 days or more delinquent' to be a Liquidated Mortgage Loan although nothing has been liquidated. The two limbs give the same defined term two incompatible senses.

'Majority in Interest' is defined in words materially identical to the separately defined 'Majority Holder' (51% of the Percentage Interests of a Class of Regular Certificates), the only difference being singular versus plural Holders. Whether the two terms mean different things where the Agreement uses them separately is left open.

The account is said to be established 'pursuant to 3.07(j) of this agreement,' a citation omitting the word Section and not verifiable against the subsection lettering used for the other Section 3.07 accounts. The establishing provision must be located by inference.

Limb (b) is itself 'the lesser of (a) the product of ... and (b) the aggregate Stated Principal Balance ... minus the OC Floor,' reusing the letters (a) and (b) that already label the outer limbs. The nesting error makes the computation ambiguous on its face.

'Mortgage' is defined as an instrument 'creating a second lien' on the mortgaged estate, yet the Agreement's Loan-to-Value Ratio, Primary Insurance Policy and foreclosure provisions all presuppose that the Trust holds the senior security. Whether the Trust's loans are first or second liens cannot be settled from this definition alone.

Items (5) and (7) require the 'Scheduled Principal Balance' of each Mortgage Loan, a term the Agreement does not define, and item (33) is simply '[reserved].' The content of the schedule on those points is indeterminate.

Mortgaged Property is confined to one- to four-family dwellings and individual condominium units, but the Agreement separately contemplates Cooperative Mortgage Loans secured by Cooperative Shares and a Proprietary Lease rather than by such real property. The definition does not accommodate the cooperative collateral the Agreement elsewhere assumes.

For the Class 1-A-3, Class 2-A-3 and Class 4-A-2 Certificates the Net Rate Cap is reduced by the Certificate Insurer Fee Rate, so the insurer's premium comes out of the insured holders' rate, while Endorsement No. 1 to the Certificate Insurance Policy excludes from Guaranteed Distributions any shortfall 'resulting from application of the Net Rate Cap.' Whether the premium-driven reduction is an insured shortfall or one the holders bear turns on reading the two instruments together.

Net Rate Carryover measures the interest lost to the Net Rate Cap for the Insured Certificates among others, but under Section 4.02 it is payable only out of Net Monthly Excess Cashflow and the Carryover Reserve Fund and is expressly outside the Guaranteed Distributions defined in Endorsement No. 1 to the Policy. Whether holders of Insured Certificates have any enforceable entitlement to it requires reading those provisions together.

'NIMS Insurer' is defined as 'any insurer' guaranteeing notes secured by certain Certificates, with no requirement that one exist, be identified, or give notice, yet the Agreement conditions numerous actions on its consent. Whether a NIMS Insurer exists at any time, and who it is, cannot be determined from the definition.

Recoverability turns on 'the good faith judgment of the applicable Servicer or the Master Servicer,' with no objective standard, evidentiary requirement or review mechanism. Whether an Advance is nonrecoverable is left to an undefined subjective test.

An Officer's Certificate may be signed only by officers of the Depositor or the Master Servicer, although the Agreement elsewhere requires certificates from the Trustee, Trust Administrator and Custodian. The definition's enumeration excludes signatories the Agreement assumes.

Counsel need only be 'reasonably acceptable to the Trustee or the Trust Administrator,' a standard with no criteria and with no indication of which of the two officers' acceptance governs. The qualification is left to be judged after the fact.

The term covers only the Senior and Mezzanine Certificates, yet the Preliminary Statement's Middle REMIC 2 notes size interests by 'the Original Certificate Principal Balance of its Corresponding Class of Certificates' for classes outside that group. The definition does not reach every class that uses it.

Outstanding is defined to include all authenticated Certificates subject only to cancellation and replacement exceptions, while the definition of Certificateholder deems Certificates held by the Master Servicer, the Depositor or their affiliates 'not to be Outstanding' for consent purposes. The two definitions must be reconciled to know what is Outstanding on a vote.
The definition breaks off at 'the Overcollateralization Target Amount for such Distribution 34', without completing the clause. The comparison that fixes the release amount is textually incomplete.

After ten enumerated categories, clause (k) permits 'such other investments bearing interest or sold at a discount acceptable to each Rating Agency,' a catch-all not limited by the character of the listed items. Its breadth against the enumerated specifics is open to argument.

Clause (vii) excludes 'any other Person so designated by the Depositor based upon an Opinion of Counsel,' a residual category resting on the Depositor's designation rather than on any stated criterion. Whether a transferee is permitted can turn on a discretionary act not otherwise constrained.

Limb (B) adds 'the Premium Distribution Amount for any prior Distribution Date, plus interest thereon at the Late Payment Rate' without limiting it to the unpaid portion, so on its face every prior period's premium is added again each month. The definition is also keyed to the Late Payment Rate, which is defined by reference to undefined 'Insured Notes' and a 'Class A Note Insurer.'

Prepayment Interest Excess is defined only as to AHM Mortgage Loans, yet the closing sentence disposes of 'All Prepayment Interest Excess' and the Interest Remittance Amount definition excludes Prepayment Interest Excess for the Mortgage Loans generally. Whether excess interest on non-AHM loans belongs to the Trust or the Servicer is unresolved between them.

The definition twice turns on whether a loan has become a 'Liquidated Loan,' a term the Agreement does not define; the defined term is 'Liquidated Mortgage Loan.' When a loan's Principal Balance drops to zero therefore rests on an undefined trigger.

The last clause directs that partial prepayments 'shall be applied in the Prepayment Period preceding the receipt thereof,' which places the application before the money arrives. The timing rule contradicts itself as written.

Clause (iii) counts 'the principal portion of all related Net Liquidation Proceeds,' a term the Agreement does not define; it defines 'Liquidation Proceeds' only. What is netted out before the proceeds reach the waterfall is left unstated.

The price includes 'any costs and damages incurred by the Trust in connection with any violation by such Mortgage Loan of any predatory or abusive lending law,' with no definition of the covered laws, of 'damages,' or of who determines them. That component of the Purchase Price has no ascertainable measure.

'Qualified Mortgage Insurer' requires only Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac approval, while the separately defined 'Qualified Insurer' imposes licensing and an 'AA' claims-paying rating for what is functionally the same insurer. Which standard governs a given Primary Insurance Policy depends on which term the operative provision uses.

The second sentence, covering a Deficient Valuation, is a fragment: it states 'the difference between the principal balance ... and the principal balance as reduced' without saying that this difference is a Realized Loss or when it is taken. The grammatical gap leaves the treatment of Deficient Valuations uncertain.

The definition covers Delay Certificates, Physical Certificates and No Delay Certificates 'held in Book-Entry Form,' leaving no Record Date for a No Delay Certificate that is not held in book-entry form. Definitive Certificates of those classes fall through the gap.

The provision says the term 'may refer to a portion of the Relevant Servicing Criteria applicable to such parties' without saying which portion or who decides. What criteria a Servicing Function Participant must assess is left open.

The definition extends beyond the cited Code sections and regulations to 'related provisions' and 'provisions of applicable state laws,' neither of which is identified. The body of law the Agreement requires be complied with is left unbounded.

'Residual Interests' is defined as 'specified in the Preliminary Statement,' but the Preliminary Statement designates the LT-R, MT1-R, MT2-R and Class R-IV interests without ever using that collective term. The referent of the definition is absent from the place it points to.

A Responsible Officer is any listed officer 'having direct responsibility for the administration of this Agreement and also to whom, with respect to a particular matter, such matter is referred because of such officer's knowledge,' so it is unclear whether both limbs must be satisfied. Whose knowledge is attributed to the Trustee or Trust Administrator turns on that reading.

If a later rule change makes certification 'in the reasonable judgment of the Master Servicer, materially more onerous,' the required certification becomes whatever the Master Servicer and Depositor agree after 'a negotiation in good faith.' The obligation is an agreement to agree with no fallback if they do not.

The Scheduled Payment gives effect to 'any related Debt Service Reduction,' a capitalized term the Agreement does not define. The adjustment to the scheduled payment therefore rests on an undefined concept.

Servicing Advances are 'all customary, reasonable and necessary out of pocket costs and expenses' incurred in servicing, with no list, cap or standard for judging custom, reasonableness or necessity. What a Servicer may advance and recoup off the top of collections is left to argument.

The list of Servicing Agreements includes '(g) the Assignment Agreements,' which are assignment, assumption and recognition agreements rather than servicing agreements. Obligations the Agreement imposes 'under the related Servicing Agreement' therefore have an uncertain referent.

The definition captures 'any Sub-Servicer or Subcontractor,' but the Agreement defines 'Subservicer' and not 'Sub-Servicer.' Whether the participant category matches the defined class of servicing delegates is left unclear.

The closing sentence provides that 'the Stated Principal Balance of a Liquidated Loan is zero,' using a term the Agreement never defines; the defined term is 'Liquidated Mortgage Loan.' The point at which a loan drops out of the balance is fixed by an undefined label.

Subsequent Recoveries are 'unanticipated amounts' received on a liquidated loan, with no test for what was anticipated or by whom. Whether a later recovery counts is a judgment the definition does not constrain.

The definition reads 'any Mortgage Loan that is purchased by the ... originator is an amount equal to the excess,' both ungrammatical and attributing the purchase to the originator, whereas Section 2.03 places substitution and repurchase on the Transferor. Who owes the adjustment amount is garbled.

The Supplemental Interest Trust is held 'for the benefit of the holders of the Senior Certificates and the Mezzanine Certificates,' while Section 2.01(f) has the Cap Contract acknowledged by holders of the Senior Certificates 'other than Group 3 Certificates' and the Mezzanine Certificates. Whether Group 3 holders are beneficiaries of the supplemental trust is not consistently stated.

Trust Administrator Compensation is all investment earnings on the Distribution Account, while Master Servicer Compensation is all investment earnings on the Collection Account and Section 2.01(e) permits the Collection Account to 'be deemed to be a sub-account of the Distribution Account.' If the deeming operates, both definitions claim the same earnings.

The corpus enumerated here omits the Carryover Reserve Fund, the Cap Contract, the Cap Account, the Mezzanine Cap Contract and the Supplemental Interest Trust, which the Preliminary Statement nonetheless treats as assets of the Trust Fund excluded from the REMICs as 'Excluded Trust Assets.' Whether those assets are in the Trust Fund at all cannot be settled from this definition alone.

The NIMS Insurer's rights are made to depend on notes 'issued pursuant to the Indenture,' but 'Indenture' is not a defined term anywhere in this Agreement and no such instrument is identified. Whether and when the NIMS Insurer holds rights cannot be determined from the provision.

The conveyance excludes 'those rights under the Servicing Agreements that do not relate to servicing of the Mortgage Loans,' including Servicer representations and warranties and remedies, 'which rights were retained by the Transferor' — with the parenthetical left unclosed. Which loan-level claims passed to the Trust and which the Transferor kept is precisely what the exclusion leaves open.

Items (B), (C) and (E) are each required only 'except as provided below,' and item (B) allows a mere copy 'certified by the related originator' in place of the original recorded Mortgage. What a complete Mortgage File must contain is therefore qualified in ways the clause does not itself specify.

Item (F) requires UCC assignments 'of the security interest referenced in clause (v) above,' but this list is lettered (A) through (H) and contains no clause (v). The document required cannot be identified from the cross-reference.

The provision states that delivery of the recorded Mortgage and interim assignments shall 'in no event' be later than one year after the Closing Date, then in the proviso allows delivery 'within 720 days following the Closing Date' for the same documents. The two outside dates cannot both control.

The recording carve-out turns on whether recordation is required 'by either Rating Agency,' although the Preliminary Statement designates three Rating Agencies, and the sentence breaks off mid-clause ('may conclusively 47'). Both the scope of the exception and the parties' reliance right are left incomplete.

The clause says only that the parties 'agree and understand that it is not intended' that any listed high-cost loan be included, which states an expectation rather than a representation or covenant, yet it supports an indemnity from the Depositor and the Trust Fund. Whether it creates an enforceable obligation at all is the question it raises.

If an account ceases to be an Eligible Account the responsible party must 'immediately' establish a new one and transfer the funds, with no cure period or notice mechanic and no consequence specified for failure. What 'immediately' requires is undefined.

This clause directs the Trust Administrator to execute, deliver and perform the Cap Contract, whereas the definition of Cap Contract describes it as a contract between the Cap Provider and the Supplemental Interest Trust Trustee. Which capacity of Wells Fargo is the counterparty must be resolved between the two.

The Custodian 'acknowledges receipt of the documents identified in the Initial Certification' rather than of the documents Section 2.01(b) requires to be delivered, so the acknowledgment measures itself by its own certification. What has actually been delivered to the Trust is not established by the acknowledgment.

The Custodian certifies 'based on its review and examination' that the documents 'appear regular on their face,' and in the next sentence is placed 'under no duty or obligation to inspect, review or examine' those same documents. The two statements pull against each other within one provision.

The Custodian must identify the originator for any Mortgage Loan 'with a material exception,' but neither 'material' nor 'exception' is defined or measured against any standard. Which exceptions trigger the disclosure duty is left open.

The Custodian must list any document that 'does not meet the requirements of Section 2.01' as an exception, yet is simultaneously barred from determining whether endorsements are sufficient, whether assignments are in recordable form, or whether certain documents belong in the file. The review duty and the carve-outs from it cover much the same ground.

The repurchase obligation arises only if the defect 'materially and adversely affects the interests of the Certificateholders or the Certificate Insurer in the related Mortgage Loan,' with no standard for materiality and no allocation of the burden of showing it. Whether a given document defect triggers repurchase is left at large.

The cure-or-repurchase obligation is declared 'the sole remedies respecting such defect available to the Trustee, the Master Servicer, the Depositor and any Certificateholder,' an enumeration that omits the Certificate Insurer and the NIMS Insurer, to whom the Agreement elsewhere gives enforcement and reimbursement rights. Whether the insurer is confined to the same sole remedy turns on that omission.

For representations made 'to the best of the Transferor's knowledge,' the provision deems an inaccuracy a breach 'notwithstanding the Transferor's lack of knowledge,' so the qualifier is given and taken away in the same sentence. What a knowledge-qualified warranty means here is the question the clause creates.

The deemed-material list runs to 'clauses (xiii), (xiv), (xv) and (xxxv) through (l) of Schedule II,' where '(l)' can be read as the roman numeral fifty or as the letter l, and the trigger elsewhere in the same paragraph shifts between the interests of the Certificateholders 'or' and 'and' the Certificate Insurer. Which representations are automatically material, and whose interests must be affected, is unclear.

This paragraph gives the Transferor ninety days from discovery or notice to cure a representation breach, while Section 2.02 imposes a separate ninety-day cure-or-repurchase regime for document defects on the same loans. Which regime governs a defect that is both is not addressed.

Here the Substitution Adjustment Amount is computed by the Master Servicer as the shortfall between substitute and deleted loan balances and is remitted by the Transferor, whereas the Section 1.01 definition frames it as arising on a Mortgage Loan 'purchased by the ... originator.' The two statements of the same defined term do not match.

The sole-remedy sentence lists 'Certificateholders, the Master Servicer, the NIMS Insurer, the Depositor, the Trust Administrator or the Trustee' but not the Certificate Insurer, whose enforcement and reimbursement rights appear in the same Section 2.03. Whether the Certificate Insurer is bound by the sole-remedy limitation is left to inference from the list.

Discovery of a breach of the Section 2.04 representations requires only prompt written notice; no cure, repurchase or substitution obligation or any other remedy is attached, unlike the Section 2.03 regime. What follows a breach of the Depositor's title warranty is unstated.

The Trustee agrees here to perform its duties 'to the best of its ability, to the end that the interests of the Holders ... may be adequately and effectively protected,' while Article VIII limits the Trustee to the duties expressly set out and negates implied covenants. The standard of the Trustee's obligation cannot be taken from this section alone.

The representation is satisfied if 'the Master Servicer or an affiliate thereof' is an approved Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac servicer and HUD-approved mortgagee, so it warrants nothing about the Master Servicer itself. What is warranted about the contracting party is left indeterminate.

The Master Servicer must act 'with customary and usual standards of practice of prudent mortgage loan master servicers' while also having 'full power and authority to do any and all things which it may deem necessary or desirable.' Neither the prudent-master-servicer standard nor the limits on that discretion is defined.

Tax and insurance costs are not to 'be added to the Scheduled Principal Balances of the related Mortgage Loans,' using a term the Agreement does not define; the defined balances are 'Principal Balance' and 'Stated Principal Balance.' The quantity that may not be increased is unnamed.

Whether a Servicer is to be terminated rests on the Master Servicer's own 'judgment,' after which it may 'issue such notice or take such other action as it deems appropriate,' with no standard or obligation fixed. The provision creates a duty measured only by the obligor's discretion.

The Master Servicer 'shall' terminate a non-performing Servicer, yet the same paragraph makes enforcement a matter of what it 'in its good faith business judgment, would require were it the owner of the related Mortgage Loans.' The mandatory and discretionary formulations of the same duty conflict within the provision.

The Master Servicer may reimburse itself from the Collection Account for termination and transfer costs 'including, without limitation' two broadly described categories, with no cap and no requirement of reasonableness. The scope of the charge against trust collections is open-ended.

The Master Servicer must evaluate a consent request 'in the best interest of the Trust and the Certificateholders' and act 'promptly or within the time frame specified in such Servicing Agreement, if any,' leaving both the standard and the deadline indefinite where the Servicing Agreement is silent. The Certificate Insurer's interest is not mentioned at all.

This section says neither the Trustee nor the Depositor has any responsibility for the Master Servicer's acts or any duty to supervise it, while Section 3.05 and Section 7.02 require the Trustee to assume the Master Servicer's obligations on a Master Servicer Event of Termination. How far the Trustee's disclaimer survives its succession duties has to be worked out between them.

The carve-outs refer to losses of the predecessor Master Servicer 'pursuant to Section 3.09 hereof' and to expenses 'pursuant to Section 2.03,' but Section 3.09 concerns access to documentation and does not deal with losses. The scope of the successor's exemption rests on miscited sections.

The Master Servicer must 'use its best efforts to effect the orderly and efficient transfer' of the subservicing agreements, a standard the Agreement neither defines nor measures. What effort discharges the duty is left open.

If the Master Servicer does not pay within thirty days the cost becomes 'an expense of the Trust' payable out of the Distribution Account, 'provided that the Master Servicer shall reimburse the Trust for any such expense' — the same obligation it has just failed to perform. The proviso leaves the Trust with a circular remedy.

Item (iii) requires deposit of 'all Recoveries,' a capitalized term the Agreement does not define (it defines 'Subsequent Recoveries'), and items (x) and (xi) refer to 'the Mortgage Loans in such Loan Group' although no Loan Group has been identified in the sentence. What must be deposited is uncertain in those respects.

Realized investment losses in the Collection Account are to be deposited by the Master Servicer 'in the Collection Account or paid to the Trust Administrator ... for deposit into the Distribution Account,' without saying who chooses between the two. The destination of the make-whole payment is left unfixed.

This subsection repeats verbatim the Eligible Account covenant already made in Section 2.01(e), including the sub-account proviso. Two identical covenants in different articles invite argument over whether they were meant to operate differently.

The Carryover Reserve Fund is held 'in trust for the benefit of the Holders of the Offered Certificates,' while the following paragraph directs its investment for the benefit of the Class C Certificateholders and provides that the Class C Certificates evidence ownership of the fund. The identity of the beneficial owner is stated two ways.

The exculpation is for investments 'made in accordance with this Section 3.05,' although the Carryover Reserve Fund and its investments are governed by Section 3.07(h) in which the sentence appears. The exculpation is tied to the wrong section.

Cap Account investments are made 'for the benefit of the Supplemental Interest Trust, on behalf of the Holders of the Offered Certificates,' yet the same paragraph provides that 'the Class C Certificates shall evidence ownership of the Cap Account' and gives the Class C Holders the investment direction. Who owns the account and its earnings is stated inconsistently.

Mezzanine Cap Account investments are made 'for the benefit of the Supplemental Interest Trust, on behalf of the Holders of the Mezzanine Certificates,' yet the same paragraph says 'the Class C Certificates shall evidence ownership of the Mezzanine Cap Account' and gives the Class C Holders the investment direction. The beneficial ownership of the account is stated two different ways.

Clause (ix)(A)(ii) requires withdrawal of 'any Recoveries received during the related Prepayment Period,' but 'Recoveries' is not a defined term in the Agreement (only 'Subsequent Recoveries' is). What must be moved to the Distribution Account is therefore uncertain.

Clause (iii) lets the Trust Administrator withdraw 'any indemnity, expense or other reimbursement owed to it or the Trustee' from the Distribution Account, ahead of and outside the distribution priorities of Section 4.02. How that self-help interacts with the certificateholders' waterfall is not addressed in either provision.

Clause (iii) allows the balance of the Carryover Reserve Fund to be distributed to the Depositor after Net Rate Carryover is paid 'on the Distribution Date in December of 2006,' although Section 3.07(h) holds that fund in trust for the Offered Certificateholders and Section 4.02 draws on it to pay Net Rate Carryover on later Distribution Dates. The early release cannot be squared with the fund's stated purpose.

The account is cleared upon 'the Cap Contract Scheduled Termination Date,' a term that does not exist in the Agreement; the defined term is 'Cap Contract Termination Date.' When the Cap Account terminates rests on an undefined date.

The clearing date is the 'Mezzanine Cap Contract Scheduled Termination Date,' which the Agreement does not define; the defined term is 'Mezzanine Cap Contract Termination Date.' The termination trigger is stated by an undefined term.

The Master Servicer must use 'its best reasonable efforts' to keep primary mortgage insurance in force, a hybrid standard the Agreement nowhere defines and which mixes two different levels of obligation. What effort satisfies the covenant is unclear.

The deposit obligation refers to amounts collected 'under any Primary Mortgage Insurance Policies,' whereas the defined term used in the rest of the section is 'Primary Insurance Policy.' Which policies' proceeds must be deposited depends on whether the two are the same.

Foreclosure is required only for loans 'as to which no satisfactory arrangements can be made for collection of delinquent payments,' with no standard of satisfaction and no decision-maker identified. When the duty to foreclose arises is left open.

REO Property must be sold 'as expeditiously as possible,' a standard with no time limit or benchmark, sitting alongside the separate three-year REMIC disposition deadline stated later in the same section. What speed the provision requires is indeterminate.

The section forbids the Master Servicer to assert 'any claim or right of setoff against ... any funds collected on ... a Mortgage Loan,' then excepts setoff for 'any amounts that are properly due and payable to the Master Servicer under this Agreement.' The exception is measured only by the Master Servicer's own view of what is properly due.

The Master Servicer may withdraw 'an amount equal to the Master Servicing Compensation,' but the Agreement defines 'Master Servicer Compensation' and not 'Master Servicing Compensation.' The measure of the fee is stated by a term that does not appear in Article I.

The Trust Administrator (and any Servicing Function Participant) must deliver an 'Officer's Certificate,' but that defined term covers only certificates signed by officers of the Depositor or the Master Servicer. Who may sign the Trust Administrator's Annual Statement of Compliance is not provided for.

The assessment must cover 'the fiscal year covered by the Form 10 K required to be filed pursuant to Section 3.22,' but Section 3.22 requires no Form 10-K; the annual report obligation is in Section 9.12. The period the assessment must address is fixed by a broken cross-reference.

The obligation survives termination under 'this Agreement, or any applicable Custodial Agreement, Servicing Agreement or sub-servicing agreement,' but 'Custodial Agreement' is not a defined term and no such separate agreement is identified. Which instrument's termination triggers the surviving duty is unclear.

The parties' obligations are to be 'supplemented and modified as necessary' to conform to amendments, 'interpretive advice or guidance, convention or consensus among active participants in the asset-backed securities markets, advice of counsel, or otherwise,' none of which is identified or limited. What duties this imposes, and on whose say-so, cannot be determined from the words.

The errors-and-omissions policy and fidelity bond need only be 'in such form and such amount generally acceptable for entities serving as master servicer,' with no amount, rating or benchmark specified. Whether coverage complies is left to an undefined market standard.

This paragraph turns on 'the Confirmation,' the 'Cap Contract Counterparty,' the 'Cap Contract Scheduled Termination Date' and 'Net Rate Carryover Amounts,' none of which is a defined term in the Agreement (which defines Cap Provider, Cap Contract Termination Date and Net Rate Carryover). The termination events, the obligor and the end date are all identified by terms the Agreement does not supply.

The final sentence directs distribution of amounts that 'remain in the Cap Account,' although the paragraph governs the Mezzanine Cap Contract and its proceeds are deposited in the Mezzanine Cap Account. Which account's residue goes to UBS Securities LLC is misstated.

The Credit Risk Manager 'may be terminated by the Depositor at the direction of Certificateholders evidencing not less than 66 2/3% of the Voting Rights' only 'if the Credit Risk Manager is no longer able to perform its duties,' while the last sentence bars any termination from taking effect until a successor is appointed and the Depositor need only appoint one 'at its option.' Whether the holders' direction can ever be given effect is unclear.

The exculpation covers action 'taken or for refraining from the taking of any action in good faith pursuant to this Agreement, in reliance upon information provided by the related Servicer ... or of errors in judgment,' a series whose last item does not fit the grammar of the sentence. The scope of the protection is garbled.

The Master Servicer's Advance obligation is subject to its own determination that an Advance would be a Nonrecoverable Advance, supported only by an Officer's Certificate stating its reasons, with no review or objective test. Whether an Advance was properly withheld cannot be tested by the provision's own terms.

The waterfall pays the Certificate Insurer its Premium Distribution Amount and Aggregate Certificate Insurer Reimbursement Amount ahead of Mezzanine interest and principal, and pays Unpaid Realized Loss Amounts on the Class 1-A-3, 2-A-3 and 4-A-2 Certificates only 'to the extent not covered by the Certificate Insurance Policy,' which requires reading the priorities against the Policy and Endorsement No. 1 and the deemed-balance proviso in the definition of Certificate Principal Balance. Whether insured holders or the insurer are entitled to a given dollar cannot be determined from this section alone.

Within each senior group, Applied Realized Loss Amounts are written down first against the insured class (Class 1-A-3, Class 2-A-3 and Class 4-A-2) before the uninsured classes, while the definition of Certificate Principal Balance deems the insured classes' balances not reduced by insurer payments 'solely' for premium and subrogation purposes. Whether a written-down insured certificate retains a claim, and against whom, only appears from reading the two together.

Subsequent Recoveries are allocated here to increase the Class Principal Balances of the Class 1-A-3, Class 2-A-3 and Class 4-A-2 Certificates, while the definition of Certificate Principal Balance provides that Subsequent Recoveries payable to those classes 'shall be payable to the Certificate Insurer' to the extent the loss was paid under the Policy. The two directions cover the same money.

The opening parenthetical directs that the principal and interest figures 'be expressed as a dollar amount per one thousand' (and is never closed), while the closing sentence of the same subsection directs that the same figures be expressed 'as a dollar amount per single Certificate of the relevant Class.' The two instructions for items (i) and (ii) contradict each other.

The Trust Administrator's responsibility 'is limited to the availability, timeliness and the accuracy of the information provided by each Servicer,' which as written makes it responsible for exactly what it evidently means to disclaim. The sentence reverses the intended limitation.

The Master Servicer must use its 'reasonable best efforts' to make a Servicer correct information, a compound standard the Agreement does not define. What that requires when a Servicer refuses is unstated.

The Supplemental Interest Trust is established for the benefit of the holders of the Senior and Mezzanine Certificates, yet Section 2.01(f) excludes the Group 3 Certificates from the Cap Contract arrangement and Sections 3.07(i) and (j) give the Class C Certificates ownership of the Cap Accounts held for that trust. Who benefits from the supplemental trust is stated differently in each place.

The priorities in this subsection are numbered (11) through (18) and then '(9) ninth,' although they are described as 'first' through 'ninth' in a self-contained sequence. The numbering does not correspond to the order or to the cross-references made to it elsewhere.

Distributions run to 'the Mezzanine Cap Contract Scheduled Termination Date,' a term the Agreement does not define; the defined date is the 'Mezzanine Cap Contract Termination Date.' The end of the distribution period is fixed by an undefined term.

The MTA fallback uses 'the Reserve Interest Rate,' a term defined only inside Section 4.10 by reference to one-month U.S. dollar LIBOR quotations, which is not a substitute for a twelve-month Treasury average. Importing that rate into the MTA determination produces a rate of a different character.

The margin adjustment is 'the difference between MTA for the final three years it was in effect and the average of the most recent three years for the replacement index,' comparing an unaveraged index figure with an average. The computation cannot be performed as literally written.

COFI is to be taken from FHLB San Francisco statistics 'as most recently available generally as of a day specified in the related note,' although the Certificates are not notes and no such day is specified anywhere. The determination date for the index is left unfixed.

The COFI fallback substitutes 'the Reserve Interest Rate,' which Section 4.10 defines by reference to one-month U.S. dollar interbank lending quotations rather than to any cost-of-funds measure. The substitute index is of a different kind from the one it replaces.

Certificates are issuable 'in the minimum denominations, integral multiples in excess thereof ... and aggregate denominations per Class set forth in the Preliminary Statement,' but the Preliminary Statement sets out class designations, rates and balances and states no minimum denominations. The authorized denominations must be found somewhere other than where this section sends the reader.

This section makes countersignature by the Trust Administrator 'conclusive evidence, and the only evidence,' that a Certificate was duly executed, while Section 11.10 speaks of the Certificates 'upon due authentication thereof by the Trustee.' Which act validates a Certificate is stated differently in the two places.

For an ERISA-Restricted Certificate that is neither a Private nor a Residual Certificate the required representation is 'deemed to have been made ... by the transferee's ... acceptance,' yet the final sentence makes any transfer to or on behalf of a Plan 'void and of no effect.' A deemed representation and an automatic voiding cannot both govern the same transfer.

The transfer restriction applies 'prior to the termination of the Interest Rate Cap Agreement,' a term the Agreement never defines; the defined instruments are the Cap Contract and the Mezzanine Cap Contract. When the restriction lapses cannot be determined.

On a violating transfer 'the next preceding permitted beneficial owner will be treated as the beneficial owner,' but 'permitted beneficial owner' is not a defined term and no register of beneficial owners of Book-Entry Certificates is maintained. Who is restored to ownership is left indeterminate.
The affidavit requirement excepts 'the Depositor of an affiliate thereof,' where 'of' appears in place of 'or.' The class of transferees exempt from the Transfer Affidavit is garbled.

The Depositor need only 'use its best efforts' to make available the information needed to compute the Section 860E(e) tax, a standard the Agreement does not define and which has no deadline. What discharges the obligation is unclear.

Residual Certificate holders are deemed to consent in advance to 'any amendment of this Agreement which ... is reasonably necessary' for the stated tax purposes, while Section 11.01 sets out the exclusive conditions and consents for amendments. Whether an amendment can be made on this deemed consent alone must be settled between the two.

Replacement of a lost Certificate requires delivery of security or indemnity to 'the Master Servicer, the NIMS Insurer and the Trust Administrator,' although Section 1.03 contemplates that there may be no NIMS Insurer at all. If none exists the condition cannot be satisfied as written.

This section lets the named parties treat the registered Person as owner 'for all other purposes whatsoever,' while the definition of Certificateholder disregards affiliate-held Certificates for consent purposes and Section 12.01 gives the Certificate Insurer the voting rights of the Insured Certificates. The deemed-owner rule cannot be applied literally alongside them.

The section is captioned as limiting the liabilities of the Depositor, the Master Servicer and the Custodian, but the text also purports to limit the liability of the NIMS Insurer, who is not a party. Whether the NIMS Insurer's obligations are governed by this section is left open by the mismatch.

The first sentence exculpates the named parties for good faith action 'or for errors in judgment,' while the proviso withdraws protection for 'negligence in the performance of duties hereunder' — a standard that would capture ordinary errors of judgment. The two halves of the same sentence set inconsistent thresholds of liability.

Clause (b) permits resignation once the Master Servicer's duties are 'no longer permissible under applicable law,' yet the closing sentence bars any resignation from taking effect until a successor acceptable to the NIMS Insurer and the Certificate Insurer assumes the duties. The permitted resignation can be blocked indefinitely by the very condition attached to it.

Condition (i) is stated in the disjunctive — the transferee '(a) shall be a Person qualified to service ... , (b) shall have a net worth of not less than $50,000,000 ... or (c) shall execute and deliver ... an assumption agreement' — so an unqualified transferee of any size can satisfy it merely by signing an assumption. Whether the three are cumulative or alternative is the question the drafting creates.

Clause (v) makes it an Event of Termination for the Master Servicer to assign or delegate 'in contravention of the provisions permitting such assignment or delegation under Section 6.04,' but Section 6.04 governs resignation; assignment and delegation are permitted by Section 6.05. The default is defined by reference to the wrong section.

The Trustee 'shall' terminate the Master Servicer for a failure under Sections 3.21 or 3.22, yet the proviso lets the Depositor 'at its sole option, but with the consent of the Trustee' grant a cure period for that same clause (vi) default. The mandatory duty and the discretionary cure cannot both be given effect.

This sentence removes the Trust Administrator automatically whenever the Master Servicer is terminated and the two are the same Person, while Section 9.07 sets out the exclusive grounds and procedure for the Trust Administrator's resignation or removal and Section 9.08 for a successor. Whether the automatic removal operates without those steps is unresolved.

The Trustee's succession is twice tied to 'the obligation to make Advances pursuant to Section 4.10,' although Section 4.10 governs the determination of LIBOR and Advances are required by Section 4.01. The core obligation the successor assumes is stated by a broken cross-reference.

This paragraph repeats verbatim the reimbursement mechanic already stated in Section 3.05, including the proviso that the defaulting Master Servicer 'shall reimburse the Trust' for the expense the Trust has just borne because it did not pay. The duplicated provisions leave both the source of payment and the remedy circular.

The prudent-person standard applies while a Master Servicer Event of Termination is uncured 'but only until such time as a successor Master Servicer shall have been appointed,' even though under Section 7.02 the Trustee itself becomes that successor. When the heightened standard ends, and whether it ends when the Trustee takes over, is unclear.

The opening sentence preserves the Trustee's liability 'for its own negligent action, its own negligent failure to act or its own willful misconduct,' while clause (i) provides that its duties are 'determined solely by the express provisions of this Agreement' with no implied covenants read against it. The scope of the negligence liability that survives the proviso is the question.

Clause (iv) requires investigation only if requested by Holders of 'not less than 25% of the Voting Rights allocated to each Class of Certificates,' which can be read as 25% of every Class or 25% in the aggregate. The threshold for compelling the Trustee to investigate is ambiguous.

The indemnity from the Trust covers four categories of loss but is followed by 'provided, that any such loss, liability or expense constitutes an "unanticipated expense incurred by the REMIC"' under the Treasury regulation, without saying whether that proviso qualifies only clause (iv) or all four. Read broadly the proviso would defeat most of the indemnity it follows.

The Trustee must have 'a credit rating of at least investment grade' without specifying whose rating, of what obligations, or by which agency. Whether the Trustee has ceased to be eligible, and must therefore resign immediately, cannot be determined from the requirement as stated.

The resignation sentence has no operative verb for its final clause — 'and acceptance by a successor trustee acceptable to the NIMS Insurer and the Certificate Insurer and in accordance with Section 8.08 meeting the qualifications set forth in Section 8.06' — so it is unclear whether successor acceptance is a condition of the resignation taking effect. The mechanics of a Trustee resignation are left incomplete.

The first sentence requires co-trustees to be 'approved by the Trustee, the Certificate Insurer and the NIMS Insurer' and says the Master Servicer and Trustee 'acting jointly shall' appoint them, while the next sentence lets the Trustee appoint alone if the others do not join within fifteen days. Whether the approvals are conditions or merely invitations is left unresolved.

The Trust Administrator is not relieved 'from liability for its own negligent action,' yet clause (i) confines its duties 'solely' to the express provisions with no implied obligations. What negligence remains actionable once implied duties are excluded is left open.

Clause (x) entitles the Trust Administrator to be reimbursed for discretionary litigation costs 'out of the Collection Account,' but Section 3.10(a) enumerates the permitted withdrawals from that account and gives that right only to the Master Servicer and Servicers. The two provisions cannot both be applied as written.

The Trust's indemnity of the Trust Administrator is qualified by the proviso that the loss 'constitutes an "unanticipated expense incurred by the REMIC"' under Treasury Regulations Section 1.860G-1(b)(3)(ii), with no indication whether that condition attaches to all three enumerated categories or only the last. The reach of the indemnity turns on that placement.

Eligibility requires 'a credit rating of at least investment grade' without identifying the rated obligations or the rating agency, yet loss of eligibility compels immediate resignation. The triggering condition has no ascertainable measure.

The resignation sentence ends with a dangling clause — 'and acceptance by a successor trust administrator in accordance with Section 9.08 meeting the qualifications set forth in Section 9.06' — with no verb saying that such acceptance is required. Whether successor acceptance conditions the resignation is left grammatically unresolved.

This paragraph provides that where the Master Servicer and Trust Administrator are the same Person 'the Depositor shall also remove the Trust Administrator' upon a Section 7.01 termination, while Section 7.01 states that in that event 'the Trust Administrator shall likewise be removed' automatically. Whether removal is automatic or requires the Depositor's act is stated both ways.

This sentence terminates the Master Servicer whenever the Trust Administrator is removed and the two are the same Person, while Section 7.01 removes the Trust Administrator whenever the Master Servicer is terminated. Read together the two provisions are circular, and neither says which removal starts the chain.

Clause (i) provides that the Trust Administrator 'may not be an Originator, Master Servicer, Servicer, the Depositor or an affiliate of the Depositor unless the Trust Administrator is in an institutional trust department,' yet the parties clause appoints Wells Fargo as both Master Servicer and Trust Administrator. Whether the incumbent satisfies its own eligibility condition depends on how that exception is read.

Additional compensation is the difference between the Trust Administrator Compensation and 'the current market rate ... as mutually determined by the Trustee and the successor Master Servicer' and 'as separately negotiated' by them. The obligation depends on a future agreement with no fallback if none is reached.

Covenant (i) reads 'receive any income attributable to any asset which is neither a "qualified mortgage" nor a "permitted investment"' — omitting the word 'not' that appears in every parallel covenant (f) through (k). As written the Master Servicer covenants to do the very thing that would disqualify the REMIC.

Clause (iii) applies 'in all other cases, or in the event that the Trustee, the Trust Administrator, the Master Servicer or the Transferor fails to honor its obligations under the preceding clause (i), (ii) or (iii)' — referring to itself as a preceding clause. The fallback for unpaid REMIC taxes is stated circularly.

The paragraph conditions the Trust Administrator's performance on other parties observing deadlines under 'the related Servicing Agreements, the Custodial Agreement or any other applicable agreement,' but no 'Custodial Agreement' is defined or identified in this Agreement. The source of the deadlines relied on is unidentified.

The Back-Up Certification is to be 'in the form attached hereto as Exhibit U,' but Exhibit U is identified in Section 9.12(b)(ii) as the schedule of parties and Additional Form 10-K Disclosure, while the Sarbanes-Oxley Certification form is Exhibit N. Which exhibit supplies the required back-up form cannot be told from the two provisions.

This paragraph requires 'the parties specified on Exhibit V' to deliver Form 8-K Disclosure Information, while Section 9.12(c)(i) says that information 'shall be reported by the parties set forth on Exhibit S hereto.' Which exhibit identifies the reporting parties is stated two ways.

The subsection breaks off mid-sentence at 'not resulting from its own negligence, bad faith or 107 of', leaving the exception to the liability disclaimer incomplete. The limit of the Trust Administrator's exculpation for late filings is unstated.

The outside date is 'the Latest Possible Maturity Date as defined in the Preliminary Statement,' but that term is defined in Section 1.01 by a formula and the Preliminary Statement merely tabulates December 25, 2046. Which date caps the trust's existence depends on which source controls.

The auction may proceed only if the price suffices to retire 'each class of notes issued pursuant to the Indenture' and amounts owed to 'the trustee under the Indenture,' but no Indenture is defined or identified anywhere in this Agreement. A condition to any Auction Sale is expressed by reference to an instrument the Agreement does not supply.

This subsection conditions the Master Servicer's purchase right on non-exercise by 'a Majority in Interest of the Class C Certificateholders, as Auction Initiator,' whereas Auction Initiator is defined as 'the Class C Certificateholder' and, failing its exercise, the Certificate Insurer. Whose inaction unlocks the Master Servicer's right is stated differently in the two places.

The Termination Price rests on an appraisal 'mutually agreed upon by the Master Servicer and the Trust Administrator' and a fair market value 'determined by the Master Servicer and the Trust Administrator,' although the parties clause makes Wells Fargo both. The apparent two-party check on the purchase price collapses into one entity valuing the assets it is buying.

Unsurrendered final distributions are paid over to UBS Securities LLC, a non-party, and 'all rights of non-tendering Certificateholders in or to such amounts shall thereupon cease hereunder, under the related Certificates and, if applicable, under the Certificate Insurance Policy,' while the Policy provides that it sets forth Financial Security's undertaking in full and cannot be modified or affected by any other agreement. Whether the PSA can extinguish a Holder's rights against the insurer is a question between the two instruments.

Clause (v) permits amendment without Certificateholder consent 'to modify, alter, amend, add to or rescind any of the terms or provisions contained in this Agreement,' subject only to an opinion of no material adverse effect that is deemed satisfied by rating agency letters, while the later paragraph of Section 11.01 requires the consent of a Majority in Interest of each affected Class for changes to Holders' rights. The open-ended power in clause (v) would swallow the consent requirement.

The provision refers to the Form 10-K 'and the Certification required to be attached thereto as referenced in Section 9.12(d),' but the certification requirement is in Section 9.12(b)(iv) and Section 9.12(d) deals with Form 15 and late or amended filings. The amendment power is defined by a broken cross-reference.

The opening words require the consent of 'the Holders of a Majority in Interest of each Class of Certificates affected thereby,' i.e. 51%, while clause (ii) requires consent of Holders of 'Percentage Interests aggregating 66%' of an adversely affected Class for the same kind of amendment. The governing consent threshold is stated twice at different levels.

The opinion condition applies to every amendment 'other than pursuant to the second preceding paragraph,' a reference whose target depends on how the long preceding paragraphs of Section 11.01 are counted. Which class of amendments escapes the opinion requirement is indeterminate.

The last sentence requires the Trustee, Custodian, Trust Administrator and Master Servicer to 'reasonably cooperate ... to enter into such amendments or modifications ... as may be necessary to comply with Regulation AB' 'notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Section 11.01,' while the rest of Section 11.01 conditions every amendment on consents and Opinions of Counsel. The override and the conditions cannot both govern a Regulation AB amendment.

Recordation may be directed only on an Opinion of Counsel 'to the effect that such recordation materially and beneficially affects the interests of the Certificateholders,' a standard of benefit that counsel is given no criteria to apply. The condition to recording the Agreement is effectively unmeasurable.

The Trust Administrator need only 'use its best efforts to promptly provide notice' of matters 'of which it has actual knowledge,' with no definition of best efforts and no duty to inquire. Whether a failure to notify a Rating Agency breaches anything is left open.

The notice schedule gives addresses for the Depositor, Master Servicer, Custodian, Trustee, Transferor, Rating Agencies, Trust Administrator and Certificate Insurer, but none for the NIMS Insurer or the Credit Risk Manager, to whom the Agreement repeatedly requires notices and consents. Where such notices must be sent is not provided for.

This section forbids assignment by the Master Servicer 'without the prior written consent of the Trustee, the Certificate Insurer and Depositor' except as provided in Section 6.02 and this section, while Section 6.05 permits the Master Servicer to sell, assign or delegate its rights in their entirety on conditions that do not include those consents. The two provisions give different answers to the same question.

The no-action clause bars any Holder from bringing 'any suit, action or proceeding ... upon or under or with respect to this Agreement' unless it first gives written notice of a Master Servicer Event of Termination and 25% of Voting Rights demand suit, even though many claims a Holder might bring have nothing to do with a Master Servicer default. Whether the clause reaches all claims or only those arising from such an Event of Termination is the question it poses.

This section speaks of the Certificates 'upon due authentication thereof by the Trustee pursuant to this Agreement,' while Section 5.01 and Section 2.06 provide that the Trust Administrator executes, authenticates and countersigns them and make countersignature 'the only evidence' of due execution. The two cannot both describe the act that makes a Certificate fully paid.

This section repeats the Regulation AB supplementation language of Section 3.22(d) but allocates the cost of additional information differently — here 'at the expense of the Depositor,' there subject to the requesting party paying the Trustee's increased extraordinary costs. Which expense rule governs the same request is unresolved between them.

The Certificate Insurer is 'deemed a third-party beneficiary of this Agreement to the same extent as if it were a party hereto' with the right to enforce its provisions, while Sections 2.02 and 2.03 declare cure, repurchase and substitution to be the sole remedies available to a list of persons that does not include the insurer, and Section 11.08 restricts suits by Holders. How far the insurer's enforcement right runs can only be answered against those provisions.

This section gives the Certificate Insurer the right to exercise 'all Voting Rights of the Holders of the Insured Certificates ... without any further consent' of those Holders, while the definitions of Certificateholder and Voting Rights allocate those rights to the registered Holders and Section 5.04 lets the parties treat the registered Person as owner for all purposes. Who votes an Insured Certificate must be resolved among these provisions.

This paragraph assumes the Holder of an Insured Certificate still exercises its own Voting Rights, subject to the insurer's prior written consent, while the preceding paragraph of Section 12.01 gives the Certificate Insurer the right to exercise all such Voting Rights without any further consent of the Holders. The same section states two inconsistent mechanisms for the same votes.

The consent requirement is tied to litigation 'pursuant to Section 8.02(a)(ix),' a clause that does not authorize litigation but merely excuses the Trustee absent indemnity, and it sits against the no-action provisions of Section 11.08 governing Holder-directed suits. What litigation the insurer can block is unclear once those provisions are read together.

This section deems every reference in the Agreement and the Certificates to the benefit of Holders to include the Certificate Insurer, while Sections 2.02 and 2.03 declare cure, repurchase and substitution to be the sole remedies of a list of persons that pointedly omits the insurer. The deeming provision and the sole-remedy lists have to be reconciled.

The Master Servicer's and Trust Administrator's duties are deemed owed to the Certificate Insurer as well as the Certificateholders, although Section 3.01 and Section 3.02 state the master servicing standard by reference to the Certificateholders and Section 6.03 limits liability to the Trust. Whose interests the Master Servicer must serve in a conflict between insurer and Holders is not addressed.

The claim is triggered when Available Funds distributable under Section 4.02 are insufficient to pay 'the Guaranteed Distributions (as defined in the Certificate Insurance Policy),' so the amount of any claim depends on Endorsement No. 1 to the Policy, which excludes shortfalls from the Net Rate Cap, prepayment interest and withholding taxes. What the Trust Administrator must claim, and what the insurer must pay, can only be worked out between the two documents.

Policy proceeds 'may not be applied to satisfy any costs, expenses or liabilities of the Master Servicer, the Trust Administrator, the Trustee or the Trust Fund,' yet the same paragraph directs that they be transferred to the Distribution Account and disbursed 'in accordance with Section 4.02,' whose priorities pay the Certificate Insurer's premium and reimbursement amounts and, through Section 3.10(b), trustee expenses. The restriction and the distribution mechanic pull against each other.

Policy proceeds are to be applied 'directly to the payment in full of the Insured Amount due on the Insured Certificates,' but 'Insured Amount' is not a defined term in this Agreement, which speaks instead of Guaranteed Distributions as defined in the Policy. The measure of what must be paid out of the Policy Payments Account is undefined.

This subsection defines 'Insolvency Proceeding' as a proceeding by or against the Depositor, while Section 1.01 already defines the same term for any Person and any of a long list of proceedings. The same defined term carries two different meanings in the instrument.

The proviso says Policy-funded payments do not 'result in the distribution or the provision for the distribution in reduction of the Class Certificate Balance of the Insured Certificates,' using a term the Agreement does not define; the defined terms are Certificate Principal Balance and Class Principal Balance. The balance that is or is not reduced by insurer payments is named by an undefined term.

The notice duty is triggered by 'the occurrence of an Event of Default,' a term the Agreement does not define; Section 7.01 defines 'Master Servicer Event of Termination' although it is captioned Events of Default. What event obliges the Trust Administrator to notify the insurer is left uncertain.

Clause (ii) defines 'Business Day' for Article XII by reference to the city of the Corporate Trust Office of the Master Servicer, Trustee or Trust Administrator, while Section 1.01 defines the same term by reference to New York City and the States of Minnesota and Maryland. Claim deadlines under the Policy turn on which definition applies.

Holders are made to acknowledge that the Policy does not cover 'Prepayment Interest Shortfalls, Net Rate Carryovers, or Relief Act Interest Shortfalls' — the last being an undefined term — even though the Policy itself provides that it sets forth Financial Security's undertaking in full and is unaffected by any other agreement, and Endorsement No. 1 states the exclusions in its own words. What the Policy covers must be settled between the two instruments.

The Trust Administrator is authorized to administer and make all payments under 'the Certificate Insurance Policy and the Indemnification Agreement,' but no Indemnification Agreement is defined or identified anywhere in this Agreement. The scope of the power of attorney granted by the Trustee is uncertain.

Payments made with Policy moneys 'shall not result in the payment of or the provision for the payment of the principal of or interest on such Insured Certificate within the meaning of Section 4.01,' although Section 4.01 governs Advances and distributions to Certificateholders are made under Section 4.02. The deeming rule that keeps the insured certificates outstanding is anchored to the wrong section.

The insurer's rights survive until it is paid all amounts 'plus interest at the Late Payment Rate,' a rate whose definition is fixed by reference to the 'Insured Notes' and a determination by the 'Class A Note Insurer,' neither of which exists in this transaction. When the insurer's rights cease therefore depends on a rate that cannot be computed.
